newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INP snaps up 190,000 W&H shares.
newsitem.headline: INP snaps up 190,000 W&H shares.

text.p: A spokesman for stockbroker BZW said on Thursday it bought 190,000 shares in New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton on the first day of a stand in the market on behalf of Independent Press Communications.
The latter, a unit of Dublin-based Independent Newspapers Plc, is bidding $11.00 per share for Wilson and Horton.
Wilson and Horton, which owns the New Zealand Herald newspaper, closed at $11.01 on turnover of 861,971 shares.

INP is attempting to buy the 54 million shares, 55 percent, it does not already control. As well as the stand in the marekt, it is making a written offer which opened on Thursday and will run at least until November 8.
The written offer is for cash or to exchange 1.375 INP shares for one W&H share up to a limit of 40 million INP shares. The exchangeable offer is on a first-come-first-served basis.
Analysts believe the exchange offer values W&H at considerably above the $11.00 cash price -- between $11.50-$12.00 -- and they are taking arbitrage opportunities.
Brokers snapping up the W&H shares to take advantage of the exchange offer accounted for most of Thursday's volume.
Some also see W&H as a safe haven against a sharp swing to the left in Saturday's general election.
BZW will be bidding at $11.00 per share on Monday no matter what the outcome of the election, one said.
